runs.failure: withBrowserDiagnostics assertNoErrors: aborted POST /api/matches and POST /api/replay-library/encounter (net::ERR_ABORTED)
runs.diagnosis: All of the test's own assertions passed; the shared gate failed the run at the end. isFatalBrowserDiagnosticEvent treats ERR_ABORTED on GET as benign but on an API WRITE as fatal ('a save cancelled by navigation is silent data loss'). The two terminal-state archive writes are fire-and-forget effects in src/components/gameplay/pages/gameSession/GameSessionPage.lifecycle.ts (persistMatchLog line ~128, persistEncounterReplay line ~167); their cancel flags suppress only the CALLBACK, not the in-flight request. Navigating to the review screen immediately cancelled them.
runs.fix: Await both archive POSTs (waitForResponse registered before the auto-resolve click) before navigating off the completed screen, and assert both .ok(). This removed the abort AND upgraded the proof: the replay POST body is the archived event log, which is now asserted to carry the custom GameCreated snapshot (step 11 above).

runs.cause: TEST (pacing) exposing the second half of the same PRODUCT observation
runs.failure: same two aborted POSTs, still fired from the /gameplay/games/:id page
runs.diagnosis: This time the awaited FIRST pair of POSTs responded OK (both .ok() assertions passed). A SECOND, duplicate pair of the same two POSTs then fired and was cancelled by my navigation. The terminal persist effects re-fire before their own guards latch, because the guard (`hasPersisted` / `alreadyFired`) is set in the resolve callback, leaving a re-render window between fire and latch.
runs.fix: After awaiting both archive responses, `await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` so any duplicate archive write also settles before navigation. No gate weakening, no suppression, no product edit.

productObservation.severity: non-blocking; pre-existing; NOT specific to custom units and NOT introduced by this node
productObservation.title: Terminal-state archive writes are fire-and-forget and can double-fire before their own guard latches
productObservation.verbatimEvidence: run-05.log events 7 and 8: '[requestfailed] page: http://localhost:3639/gameplay/games/e8a61574-99ca-42ba-8077-9d584ed63847?campaignId=campaign-1789484407211-wdsqnd7&missionId=mission-launch-1789484405867-0 / request: POST http://localhost:3639/api/matches / resource: fetch / failure: net::ERR_ABORTED' and the identical entry for 'POST http://localhost:3639/api/replay-library/encounter'. In that same run the FIRST pair of those POSTs had already responded 2xx (both .ok() assertions passed), so these are DUPLICATE writes, not the primary ones.
productObservation.analysis: Both effects fire on the completed-session transition and are not awaited; their `cancelled` flags suppress the callback but not the in-flight fetch. The guard that prevents re-fire is set in the resolve callback, so a re-render between fire and resolve issues a second identical POST. A user who navigates off the completed screen quickly can have an archive write cancelled. The replay route documents server-side dedup for the duplicate case (src/pages/api/replay-library/encounter.ts header: it short-circuits on an already-present gameId), which is why the duplicate is benign today.
productObservation.whyNotStopped: The instruction to STOP applies if the route cannot complete with a real server-saved custom unit. The route completes: the custom identity, the custom construction seed, the terminal outcome, the post-battle campaign application, and the cold-reloaded roster all verified green. This observation concerns auxiliary replay/match ARCHIVE writes on a path shared identically by canonical units (encounter-combat-continuity.spec.ts drives the same chain but does not use withBrowserDiagnostics, which is why it never surfaced there). No product code was touched.
productObservation.recommendation: Worth its own capped follow-up per roadmap acceptance line 2 ('assign any revealed product repair its own spec and capped PR') -- latch the guard synchronously at fire time rather than in the resolve callback, and/or await the archive writes before allowing navigation. postReviewRerun.whyRerunWasNeeded: The reviewer's mandated live run failed with 'Campaign E2E stores are not exposed'. Root cause (infra, not spec): the pre-commit hook runs a BARE `npm run build`, which rebuilt the worktree WITHOUT NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE=true and replaced the E2E standalone bundle produced for the original runs. BUILD_ID on disk at review time was 1789484830850 (non-E2E), not the 1789483405493 this evidence file originally cited. Known infra note: preCommitBuildNotE2E.
postReviewRerun.mechanismVerifiedInSession: NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are INLINED at build time, so the runtime webServer.env cannot re-enable them. Confirmed by reading the built bundle: in the non-E2E build, .next/static/chunks/pages/_app-6ac683586aa1c45c.js contained `"true"===X.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE&&(window.__E2E_MODE__=!0,window.__ZUSTAND_STORES__=...)` with NO NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE assignment anywhere in the bundle (property undefined at runtime, gate permanently closed). After the E2E rebuild, _app-3ffac9f0421f4163.js contains `window.__E2E_MODE__=!0,window.__ZUSTAND_STORES__={...}` with the conditional dead-code-eliminated entirely -- positive proof the new bundle is a genuine E2E build.
